notes: Fresh checks for the supply_risk tool (20 Nov 2026). Not part of the gate.

questions.q: Which critical minerals have the highest geopolitical supply risk?
questions.judge: Calls the supply-risk tool (league table) and ranks mineral stages from its output (gallium, niobium, bismuth, tungsten and natural graphite at the top by restriction-weighted HHI). Explains in plain words that the ranking combines concentration of production with the share of supply from producers with export controls in force in 2024, and that several top entries rest on licensing only, which may be routine or work as a ban. Mentions that measures after 2024 are not in the score (documents may be cited for them). Does not cite World Bank governance scores, give probabilities or forecast prices. No invented figures.

questions.q: How exposed is the EU to export-controlled cobalt supply?
questions.judge: Uses the supply-risk tool for cobalt with the EU as importer; reports that the DRC (about 73% of mine supply) has a ban or quota in force and that about 90% of world mine supply comes from producers with export controls; gives the EU's extra-EU imports of the stage's products and the share from controlled exporters (about 20%) with main suppliers, and EU import reliance (81% primary, 1% refined) and recycling rate (22%) from the 2023 CRM assessment. May note that the EU mostly buys refined cobalt made elsewhere (e.g. China) so direct exposure understates indirect dependence. No probability or price forecast; no invented figures.

questions.q: How risky is US natural graphite supply?
questions.judge: Uses the supply-risk tool for graphite with the United States as importer; reports China's share of natural graphite mine production (about 78%) with licensing controls in force (China's December 2023 licensing), the HHI or restriction-weighted HHI, and that about 63% of US natural graphite imports in 2022-2024 came from China, naming other suppliers (Canada, Mozambique, Madagascar, Mexico). Notes synthetic graphite/anode material is not covered if relevant. No probability or price forecast; no invented figures.
